question: Diagonals of a parallelogram ABCD intersect each other at the point O. If ∠AOB = 70°, ∠DAC = 32° and ∠DBC = y, then the value of 2y + 15° is :
solution:
**Calculation :**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd10ad448def9b71db99600ae6ac2d78da7423d5574f7186f1d060b924991aa7.png] 

⇒ ∠DAC = ∠ACB (Alternate angle)

⇒ ∠AOB + ∠BOC = 180° 

⇒ ∠BOC = 110° 

Now, ∠BOC + ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 180° 

⇒ ∠OBC = 180° - 110° - 32° 

⇒ ∠OBC = 38° 

⇒ ∠OBC = ∠DBC = 38° 

Now, 2y + 15° = 2 × 38° + 15° = 76° + 15° = 91° 

**∴ The correct answer is 91°**
